text:
alex: Heads-up — started seeing a big spike in kubelet-triggered evictions on the gpu nodepool in us-west-2 around now. ~40 pods evicted over the last 10m, mostly training-canary jobs. Logs show repeated netprobe timeouts and NodeCondition toggles.

infra-bot: node/gpu-usw2-0 kubelet: net-probe: timeout waiting for probe response (retry 3)
infra-bot: node/gpu-usw2-1 kubelet: marking node NotReady -> reason=NetworkUnhealthy

maya: ok how widespread? only a single AZ or entire pool? any MTU errors in dmesg?

alex: seems concentrated on the pooled nodes with Mellanox NICs, 3 nodes in az-a and 2 in az-b. dmesg includes "NETDEV WATCHDOG" and some rdma fw reset logs.

tanvi: we rotated kernel on that pool last night (6.5.3). I pushed a small RDMA FW update with the vendor driver. Could be interaction.

simon: can you paste `ip link show` and `ethtool -S` for one of the affected nodes? want to check MTU and dropped counters.

alex: pasted snippets below:
``n
$ ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd ee ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i drop
rx_dropped: 4102
tx_dropped: 0
rx_missed: 0
``n
maya: MTU looks jumbo (9000). Do we have any calico/eni/eni-plugin changes? if anything between host and overlay mismatches, netprobe can fail intermittently.

tanvi: We didn't touch CNI. However the kernel update included a new mlx5 driver that may reset queues after link flaps. That could cause short window where netprobe can't reach kubelet's local probe endpoint.

simon: short flaps will trigger kubelet's network health probe and then evict if it's configured aggressively. What's our kubelet net-probe timeout right now?

alex: kubelet args from one affected node: `--node-status-update-frequency=10s --max-pods=110 --network-plugin=cni --pod-eviction-timeout=2m` net probe implemented in our custom healthcheck runs at 5s with 3 retries (so ~15s).

maya: for emergency mitigation we can: 1) increase probe timeout/retry window 2) cordon/upgrade rollback of the kernel on problematic nodes 3) temporarily disable the aggressive netprobe in kubelet config.

ops-lead: prioritize minimal blast radius. Proposal: patch kubelet config for the pool to double probe timeout (so it tolerates 30s of flapping), cordon the two worst nodes, roll kernel back on those two, and run a small soak test. If probe timeouts drop, uncordon.

simon: agree. I'll prepare a kubelet-config patch. We can use the nodepool label selector to target only the gpu pool. Plan: deploy patch via our cluster-bootstrap (kubelet configmap) with rolling restart of kubelet systemd unit using daemon rollout in 1-hour window.

tanvi: I'll schedule kernel rollback for the two nodes with the highest drops after we patch kubelet. Also will open vendor ticket for mlx5/rdma resets.

alex: quick workaround idea — create a short-lived DaemonSet that reduces `net.ipv4.tcp_retries2`? Not ideal. I'd rather change kubelet probe settings so we don't get noisy evictions.

maya: +1. Evictions are painful for training queues; losing 40 pods costs us GPU-hours and increases churn. Make sure we add cost impact in the incident notes.

ops-lead: timeline: (a) simon — PR for kubelet probe timeout change in 15m, (b) infra team — apply to gpu nodepool, (c) tanvi — rollback kernels on two nodes after patch, (d) monitor for 1h, (e) postmortem if behavior persists.

infra-bot: incident created: #INC-2026 netprobe-evict-usw2, severity=high, owner=simon, runbook=netprobe-evictions.md

alex: noted. I'll collect pod evict/creation timestamps and cost estimate and drop into the incident doc. Anyone see any objections to the plan?

maya: none. please include exact kubelet arg changes in the PR. Also add a temporary alert mute for that nodepool's pod-eviction count so pager doesn't churn while we hotfix.

simon: will do. PR will include reversible kubelet ConfigMap change and rollout steps.

tanvi: opening vendor ticket and will attach dmesg/driver logs.

ops-lead: thanks team. After we stabilize, let's add an automated canary test for RDMA NICs during kernel/driver upgrades so this doesn't surprise us again.

alex: agreed. Thanks all — I'll update the incident doc and ping when evictions stop. :thumbsup:
